Elena — thanks, appreciate the clarity. I attached a short MAP (BlueHarbor_MAP_v2.xlsx) with proposed milestone dates and owners; summary below. My aim is to create a strict signature runway (3 calendar weeks) but with two conditional fallbacks so BlueHarbor's procurement team has an option to close on commercial terms while legal finishes redlines.

Proposed milestones (high level):
- Week 0 (today): Share MAP + preliminary order form (done)
- Week 1 (target): Legal redline review (Redwood legal) — DPA focused
- Week 1–2: Evidence session — SOC2 walkthrough + sample auditor notes (30–45min session)
- Week 2: Negotiation window (commercial team & procurement) — final order form numbers
- Week 3: Signature window — primary: MSA + DPA + Order Form via DocuSign
- Pilot acceptance gate: 30 days after signature (acceptance criteria documented in MAP tab)

Conditional fallbacks:
A) If DPA redlines extend beyond Week 2, we can allow signature on order form + PO for initial pilot while legal completes DPA. In that case we lock data residency and logging SLOs in a short addendum to the order form.
B) If SOC2 evidence review uncovers a gap, we delay production traffic but allow a limited pilot under a sandbox agreement with explicit data processing limits.

I've cc'd Laura for legal alignment and Karthik for procurement sequencing (PO/process). Attached: BlueHarbor_MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP + milestone matrix) and a one-page summary for procurement.

Next steps: 1) Laura to confirm DPA review owner and expected turnaround; 2) BlueHarbor to confirm preferred date range for SOC2 session (we have availability next Tue/Wed 10–11am PT); 3) Karthik to confirm internal DocuSign workflow and whether procurement will accept signature + PO fallback.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk the MAP.

- We can aim for a 7–10 business day redline turnaround if BlueHarbor can confirm a small set of non-negotiables up front (data residency, subprocessor list requests, and indemnity cap).
- I uploaded a tracked-redline PDF (DPA_redlines_2026-06-24.pdf) — this contains our suggested alternative language for Section 4 (Data Subprocessors) and Section 9 (Liability).

Those two items must be approved by our security team before we accept PO-only.
